executive_summary.text: Unknown threat actors abused a compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup credential to sign in to 173 Microsoft 365 customer tenants, forcing ConnectWise to take Cloud Backup, SaaS Security, and Cloud Management offline while investigating whether stolen tokens still grant access to client environments.

An intruder reached a legacy OpenCode system on the night of October 16 and may have exposed OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google API keys saved by users of the hosted OpenCode Console, with the breach also tied to AI distillation attacks run against customer provider accounts.

Rank Math PRO, a paid WordPress SEO plugin, distributed a self-restoring backdoor from the official rankmath.com site and through automatic updates during an 11-hour supply-chain window on October 15-16, infecting every site that installed or updated version 3.0.123 in that period.
CISA added actively exploited BeyondTrust Remote Support authentication bypass CVE-2026-102764 to its KEV catalog on October 16, triggering BOD 26-04 remediation requirements for federal agencies.
Fortinet path traversal CVE-2025-61624, also added to the KEV catalog on October 16, has been linked to a stealthy and persistent FortiGate implant deployed against a telecommunications organization.

cyber_news.title: Hackers Exploit Plex2Shell Flaws to Install Crypto Miners and Linux Proxy Backdoor
cyber_news.summary: Threat actors began exploiting a chain of Plex Media Server vulnerabilities just one day after a proof-of-concept went public, deploying cryptocurrency miners and reverse proxy software on compromised servers. The in-the-wild activity was surfaced by researcher boredhackerblog.
cyber_news.expanded: The Plex2Shell chain stitches multiple Plex Media Server flaws into a pre-auth remote code execution path, and mass exploitation began within roughly 24 hours of the PoC's publication. Observed payloads include a cryptocurrency miner and a Linux reverse-proxy backdoor that lets attackers relay traffic through the compromised host, useful for laundering malicious connections or reselling proxy access. The speed from disclosure to weaponization mirrors classic internet-exposed self-hosted software patterns: hobbyist media servers, often unmanaged and unpatched, became monetization infrastructure almost immediately.

cyber_news.title: Popular WordPress SEO Plugin Rank Math PRO Hijacked to Deliver Self-Restoring Backdoor
cyber_news.summary: Copies of Rank Math PRO downloaded from rankmath.com or delivered as automatic updates between 20:02 UTC on October 15 and 07:12 UTC on October 16 contained malware. Any site that installed or updated version 3.0.123 during that window was infected with a backdoor that reinstalls itself when removed.
cyber_news.expanded: The attackers compromised Rank Math's distribution pipeline so the malicious build shipped through two channels simultaneously: fresh downloads from the official site and the WordPress auto-update mechanism, which pushed the trojanized 3.0.123 package to existing installs without any admin action. The embedded backdoor is self-restoring, using WordPress hooks and scheduled events to re-inject its files and re-establish access after cleanup attempts. Because the payload arrived inside a legitimately signed, trusted plugin update, it bypassed integrity expectations entirely, and the 11-hour distribution window makes infection timing the key forensic pivot for identifying affected sites.

cyber_news.title: Hackers Hijack AOMEI Update Servers to Secretly Spread Malware
cyber_news.summary: Attackers compromised AOMEI's servers to distribute malware through a built-in promotional feature in its backup software. The tampering was brief and the configuration files were restored to their original state afterward to hide the attack.
cyber_news.expanded: The intrusion abused a legitimate promotional/offers feature in AOMEI Backupper that pulls configuration from AOMEI-controlled servers: the attackers modified the server-side configuration to push malware installers to endpoints running the backup product. Crucially, the malicious configuration was only in place briefly before being reverted to its clean state, a deliberate anti-forensics choice that leaves a narrow detection window and makes server-side logs the primary evidence source. AOMEI Backupper's large install base among home users and small businesses makes the promotional channel a high-yield distribution vector that inherits the vendor's trust.

cyber_news.title: Drupal Warns of Fast Exploitation Risk for Critical Core RCE Flaw
cyber_news.summary: Drupal patched two critical vulnerabilities allowing remote code execution on any supported version of the CMS, and warned that exploits may emerge soon. The flaws affect the Entity List and Field UI modules, with additional exploit paths through contributed modules.
cyber_news.expanded: The critical flaws live in Drupal core's Entity List and Field UI modules, and Drupal's security team explicitly flagged that exploit paths also exist through contributed modules, dramatically widening the attack surface beyond stock core installs. The bugs permit remote code execution on any supported Drupal version, and patches were shipped with an unusual explicit warning that exploitation may follow quickly. That caution is grounded in history: Drupalgeddon-era core RCEs saw mass automated exploitation within days of disclosure, and the contributed-module angle means attackers can reach sites even where the vulnerable core modules are not directly exposed.

cyber_news.title: F5 Releases Out-of-Band Patches for Critical NGINX Vulnerabilities
cyber_news.summary: F5 shipped out-of-band security patches for multiple NGINX web server flaws, including three critical-severity vulnerabilities that allow attackers to execute code on vulnerable systems.
cyber_news.expanded: The fixes landed outside F5's normal release cycle, which the vendor typically reserves for flaws it considers urgent enough to not wait for the scheduled cadence. Three of the vulnerabilities are rated critical and enable remote code execution against vulnerable NGINX deployments. NGINX's role as edge and reverse-proxy infrastructure makes these particularly consequential: a compromised instance sits in front of application tiers, terminates TLS, and inspects all proxied traffic, giving an attacker both a code-execution foothold and a privileged vantage point over everything behind it.

cyber_news.title: Hackers Exploit SiteGuard WAF Flaw to Run Commands as Root
cyber_news.summary: Attackers are actively targeting an OS command injection vulnerability in SiteGuard Server Edition that lets them execute commands with root or SYSTEM privileges on affected servers.
cyber_news.expanded: The vulnerability is an OS command injection in SiteGuard Server Edition, and exploitation is already occurring in the wild. The impact is amplified by the product's role: SiteGuard is a WAF designed to sit inline and inspect application traffic, so injected commands run with root (Linux) or SYSTEM (Windows) privileges on the very appliance guarding the application it protects. Command injection at that privilege level typically yields full host takeover, and because the WAF is positioned at the network edge, it is frequently internet-reachable by design, making it a prime initial-access target.

cyber_news.title: GhostAction Attackers Plant Credential Stealer Disguised as Font in 94 GitHub Repositories
cyber_news.summary: The threat actor behind the GhostAction supply-chain attack has expanded from injecting malicious GitHub Actions workflows into compromised projects to phishing open-source developers, planting a credential stealer disguised as a font file across 94 GitHub repositories.
cyber_news.expanded: GhostAction's first stage poisoned CI/CD by injecting malicious GitHub Actions workflows into compromised projects, abusing trusted build infrastructure to run attacker code. The newly documented evolution, detailed by OpenSourceMalware, pivots to the humans: fake font files that are actually stealer malware, distributed across 94 GitHub repositories to phish open-source developers. The campaign illustrates a compounding supply-chain pattern, where compromised maintainer accounts cascade downstream, and developer workstations, rich in tokens, SSH keys, and repository access, become the true target rather than the code itself.

cyber_news.title: 'AdFection' Turns Ad Impressions Into Zero-Click Spyware Delivery
cyber_news.summary: Spyware vendors are abusing targeted ad bidding in the digital advertising ecosystem to identify and track individuals and organizations of interest, delivering spyware through ad impressions with no user click required.
cyber_news.expanded: The AdFection technique abuses real-time bidding (RTB) infrastructure: spyware vendors purchase ad impressions targeted at specific individuals, and the ad creative itself carries the spyware payload, making delivery zero-click. The ad-tech ecosystem's granular targeting data doubles as a surveillance tool for identifying marks, while delivery rides on legitimate advertising infrastructure and domains, evading conventional web filtering and reputation systems. The technique effectively converts the programmatic ad chain, already criticized for privacy leakage via bid-stream data, into an active spyware distribution and targeting platform.

cyber_news.title: Exploited Fortinet Bug Linked to Stealthy FortiGate Implant in Telecom Hack
cyber_news.summary: A persistent, stealthy FortiGate implant was deployed against a telecommunications organization, and researchers have linked the intrusion to an actively exploited Fortinet vulnerability now listed in CISA's KEV catalog.
cyber_news.expanded: The implant was purpose-built for FortiGate edge devices and is described as both persistent and stealthy, indicating custom tooling rather than commodity malware. FortiGate appliances are high-value targets because they terminate VPNs, enforce policy, and hold network-wide credentials and configuration, so a resident implant grants durable network access without re-exploitation. Telecom targeting plus implant sophistication points toward an espionage-motivated, capable actor, and the link to the KEV-listed path traversal bug suggests initial access came through an unpatched edge device rather than credential theft.

cyber_news.title: DHS to Ban DeepSeek from Federal Civilian Agencies
cyber_news.summary: DHS will ban DeepSeek from federal civilian agencies, with the order citing national security concerns including data being sent to servers in China, the potential for malware, and overall risk to federal IT systems.
cyber_news.expanded: The ban order cites three rationales: user data transiting servers in China, the potential for malware distribution through the app, and systemic risk to federal IT environments. It continues a pattern of escalating US government action against Chinese-origin AI applications on government devices, following earlier state-level prohibitions and reflecting intelligence-community concerns that consumer AI apps double as data-collection platforms. The directive also creates downstream pressure on contractors and federally-funded entities, where compliance-driven removal of the app from managed fleets typically follows agency-level bans.

cyber_news.title: MITRE ATT&CK v20 Catalogs AI Abuse, MFA Bypass, Water Utility Attacks
cyber_news.summary: MITRE released ATT&CK v20, adding coverage for AI abuse, MFA bypass techniques, and attacks against water utilities, with 15 new detection strategies backed by 38 analytics.
cyber_news.expanded: ATT&CK v20 expands the knowledge base to catalog techniques for abusing AI systems, bypassing MFA, and attacking water utilities, reflecting the incident patterns defenders actually faced this cycle. The release ships 15 new detection strategies, six for Enterprise and nine for ICS, backed by 38 analytics, giving detection engineers ready-made content to map telemetry against emerging TTPs. The ICS emphasis is notable: water utility attacks have moved from theoretical concern to documented incident class, and the new ICS detection content targets the engineering-level access paths those intrusions follow.

cyber_news.title: Unpatched Broadcom Wi-Fi Flaw Lets Attackers in Range Run Code as Root on Routers
cyber_news.summary: A flaw in Broadcom's Wi-Fi setup software lets an attacker within radio range run code as root on Broadcom-based routers, without the network password or any pairing step. Researcher Quentin Kaiser disclosed the bug on October 16 and demonstrated it against home gateways from three vendors.
cyber_news.expanded: The vulnerability lives in Broadcom's Wi-Fi setup/provisioning software and requires no authentication whatsoever: no network password, no pairing, no user interaction, just physical proximity to the target device. Kaiser demonstrated the attack executing code as root against home gateways supplied by three different vendors, showing the flaw is systemic to the Broadcom reference stack rather than a single vendor's implementation. The bug remains unpatched, meaning any Broadcom-based consumer or SMB router within radio range is potentially exposed, and the attack path entirely bypasses the perimeter logic that assumes the Wi-Fi password is the boundary.

deep_dive.title: ConnectWise Supply-Chain Attack: Compromised Cloud Backup Credential Exposes 173 Microsoft 365 Tenants
deep_dive.content: ConnectWise disclosed that unknown threat actors obtained unauthorized access to its application identities and used a compromised Microsoft 365 credential belonging to ConnectWise Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) to authenticate into customer environments, with Huntress confirming suspicious sign-ins across 173 Microsoft 365 tenants. Because the credential belongs to a trusted vendor service rather than an individual user, the access sidestepped the normal identity trust model: inside each tenant, the activity presented as legitimate third-party application behavior rather than anomalous user logins. ConnectWise has disabled seven of its application identities and taken Cloud Backup, SaaS Security, and Cloud Management fully offline while validating whether stolen tokens still grant attackers access to client data. The incident is a textbook supply-chain compromise of MSP tooling: a single pooled service credential cascaded into hundreds of downstream customer environments. The threat actors remain unidentified and the investigation is ongoing.

biggest_hacks.title: Hackers breach Microsoft 365 tenants via ConnectWise supply-chain attack
biggest_hacks.summary: Attackers abused a compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup credential to sign in to 173 Microsoft 365 customer tenants, forcing ConnectWise to take Cloud Backup, SaaS Security, and Cloud Management offline.

biggest_hacks.title: OpenCode Console Breach May Have Exposed OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google API Keys
biggest_hacks.summary: An intruder reached a legacy OpenCode system on the night of October 16 and may have exposed third-party AI provider keys that users saved in OpenCode Console, the project's optional hosted workspace service.

biggest_hacks.title: Bullhorn takes staffing platform offline to contain cyberattack
biggest_hacks.summary: Staffing software company Bullhorn disabled access to its entire platform to contain a cyberattack that caused a system-wide outage for its customers.

biggest_hacks.title: One Compromised Login Exposed Millions of California Students' Records
biggest_hacks.summary: Intruders used a single set of compromised credentials to access an ETS SFTP server and copy records of millions of California students dating back to 2006.

biggest_hacks.title: Conduent Agrees to Pay $80m to Settle Data Breach Class Action
biggest_hacks.summary: Conduent agreed to pay $80 million to settle a class action lawsuit over a 2024 cyber incident that exposed the healthcare data of 62 million people.

DLL side-loading weakness in Siemens Software Center abused in ClickFix social-engineering attacks, pairing a genuine signed copy of the installer with malicious DLLs to infect Windows PCs.
Chain of Plex Media Server vulnerabilities weaponized within a day of public PoC disclosure to deploy cryptocurrency miners and a Linux reverse-proxy backdoor on internet-exposed servers.
